clue.text: Spring mattress by vehicle to river Nile, maybe

indicators.note: 'maybe' says the river's name is only one possible form of these letters, so another ordering is wanted

blocks.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
the letters of the river's name rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes loading a sprung mattress onto a vehicle bound for the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season or a coil inside the mattress; the whole phrase describes something you bounce on.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a taut sheet on springs that people bounce on, effectively a springy mat.

clue.text: He's just engaged to a bird, I note

blocks.note: the rook is a black bird of the crow family
taken as written
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A man has just got engaged to a girl, and the speaker remarks on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' looks like betrothal but means newly taken on for a job; 'bird' is also British slang for a girlfriend, which feeds the false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer or recruit, someone only recently hired or enlisted.

clue.text: Characteristic of those due to be worldly heirs

definitions.text: Characteristic of those due to be worldly heirs

blocks.clueFragment: Characteristic of those due to be worldly heirs
blocks.note: surface reading: the trait of rich heirs waiting for a worldly fortune
setter's reading: the Beatitude says those of this mild character shall inherit the earth

explanation.surface: A description of the typical trait of people set to inherit a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sermon on the Mount says 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth', so the meek are heirs to the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Meekness is the quality of being humble and gentle, the virtue the Beatitude promises the earth to.

clue.text: Hospital visitor in some trouble

blocks.note: surface reading: a friend calling on someone in a ward
setter's reading: the visitor is ailing and comes for treatment without staying the night

explanation.surface: Someone visiting a hospital is having some sort of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hospital visitor' usually means someone bringing grapes; here the visitor is the one with the ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: An out-patient attends hospital for treatment of a complaint but is not admitted to stay overnight.

clue.text: In church parties they could be little pests

blocks.note: taken as written
sects are breakaway groups or factions within a church

explanation.surface: Within church factions, certain members can be minor nuisances.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'little pests' seem to be troublesome parishioners, but they are literal small creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Many insects, such as aphids and weevils, are small creatures regarded as pests by gardeners and farmers.

clue.text: Form of life in ancient Rome

definitions.text: Form of life in ancient Rome

blocks.clueFragment: Form of life in ancient Rome
blocks.note: surface reading: a way of living or some creature found in the classical city
setter's reading: the Latin word meaning 'to be', the root sense of existence

explanation.surface: A historian describes a lifestyle or living creature of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' suggests a kind or sort; it is a word-form, the Latin infinitive meaning 'to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esse is Latin for 'to be', and in English philosophy it means existence or essential being.

clue.text: Rising artist from the north is concerned with trees

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
boreal means northern, from Boreas the north wind

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming northern painter turns out to be interested in trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal is the adjective for things relating to trees or living in them, like squirrels and monkeys.

clue.text: Sedate character of teams of judges?

blocks.note: surface reading: a calm person associated with panels of judges
setter's reading: judges are proverbially sober, and teams are sides

explanation.surface: A staid personality is said to belong to panels of judges.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'sober as a judge' makes judges sober, and a team is a side, so teams of judges become 'sober sides'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobersides is an old-fashioned term for a serious, solemn person who rarely laughs.

clue.text: From more than one angle 3 sound scheme

blocks.note: first meaning: solid or three-dimensional, viewed from two points as in a stereoscope
second meaning: a sound system reproducing audio through two channels

explanation.walkthrough: The stray '3' appears to be a printing slip in the source and plays no part in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, from Greek for solid, describes both three-dimensional imaging and two-channel audio reproduction.

clue.text: Favours diminutive flowers?

blocks.note: first meaning: ribbon badges worn as a sign of support or awarded as prizes
second meaning, playful: the suffix -ette makes things small, so little roses

explanation.walkthrough: 'Favours' looks like a verb but is the noun: a favour is a knot of ribbon worn as a badge.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosettes are circular ribbon decorations worn as party badges, and the word literally means small roses.

clue.text: Always, always on the increase

blocks.note: ever means at all times, as in 'ever ready'
more means greater in amount, growing

explanation.surface: Something is constantly, unendingly growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore means for all future time, forever, the poetic equivalent of the adverb given.

clue.text: The days of this wolf are past ?

definitions.text: The days of this wolf are past ?

blocks.clueFragment: The days of this wolf are past
blocks.note: surface reading: a breed of wolf that is now extinct
setter's reading: the wolf's prefix is also a past tense of the verb to be

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes that a particular kind of wolf belongs to history.
explanation.walkthrough: The wolf is a werewolf; its first four letters also form the plural past tense of 'be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Were is the past tense of 'be' used with plural subjects, and the first part of the legendary wolf-man.

clue.text: Congratulations on having a good address!

definitions.text: Congratulations on having a good address!

blocks.clueFragment: Congratulations on having a good address!
blocks.note: surface reading: praise for living somewhere smart
setter's reading: an address is a speech, and the speaker is being praised for delivering it

explanation.surface: Someone is congratulated on living at a desirable location.
explanation.walkthrough: An address can be where you live or a formal speech; here it is the speech, praised with 'well spoken!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-spoken describes someone who speaks clearly and in a refined, articulate manner, worthy of applause.

clue.text: Proof that one has right to a peerage?

definitions.text: Proof that one has right to a peerage?

blocks.clueFragment: Proof that one has right to a peerage?
blocks.note: surface reading: documents establishing a claim to be a lord
setter's reading: legal papers proving ownership of land, playfully read as the papers of a titled person

explanation.surface: Someone seeks papers proving entitlement to sit among the nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: A peer holds a title, so 'titled deeds' would prove it; the real phrase means documents proving property ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Title deeds are the legal documents proving a person's ownership of land or a house.

clue.text: Free peat came in a poor state

indicators.note: being in a poor state means being in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some free peat arrived in bad condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like an adjective describing the peat, but it is a verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate is to set free from slavery or restriction, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Ten-foot sea-creature potted for food

blocks.note: surface reading: a monster three metres long
setter's reading: a decapod crustacean with ten feet, caught in pots and eaten

explanation.surface: A giant sea monster is caught and preserved for eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten-foot' suggests size, but it means having ten feet; 'potted' refers to the pots it is trapped in.
explanation.definitionFit: The lobster is a ten-legged marine crustacean caught in lobster pots and prized as food.

clue.text: Short gin cocktail before RAF operation

definitions.note: describes the thing by when it happens: a session held before a mission

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the drink's letters are mixed up

blocks.note: brief means short in duration
the drink's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A quick gin cocktail is taken before an air force mission.
explanation.walkthrough: The gin looks like a drink for the aircrew, but it only supplies its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefing is the meeting where aircrew receive instructions immediately before flying a mission.

clue.text: Ruined by old-fashioned laundry gear

definitions.note: describes the past participle: put through the machine

blocks.note: first meaning: badly damaged or spoilt
second meaning: pressed through a mangle, the rollers once used to wring washing

explanation.walkthrough: A mangle is a hand-cranked pair of rollers once used to squeeze water out of wet laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangled means mutilated or badly spoilt, and literally means having been pressed through a mangle.

clue.text: Lover of music, this don

blocks.note: surface reading: a university lecturer fond of music
setter's reading: the seducer whose title is Don, hero of a Mozart opera

explanation.surface: An Oxford tutor is described as a music enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' suggests an academic, but it is the Spanish title in Don Giovanni, Mozart's opera about a famous lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Giovanni is the Italian name of the legendary seducer Don Juan, a lover set to music by Mozart.

clue.text: Property achieves results

blocks.note: first meaning: personal belongings, as in a dead person's personal belongings listed by a solicitor
a third meaning used as the joining verb: to bring something about
second meaning: outcomes or consequences

explanation.walkthrough: 'achieves' is a third meaning, since to effect is to bring about, so the clue offers the word three ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun covers both a person's belongings and the consequences produced by causes.

clue.text: Describing Thomas Huxley's 73 "organized common sense

blocks.note: surface reading: a reference to a quotation by the Victorian biologist
setter's reading: Huxley called science 'trained and organized common sense', so the adjective is wanted

explanation.surface: A quiz about how Huxley described a particular pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: T. H. Huxley wrote that science is 'nothing but trained and organized common sense'; the '73' appears to be a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientific means relating to science, the discipline Huxley characterised as systematised everyday reasoning.

clue.text: Chooses the wrong spot

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the following word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone picks the incorrect location.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to make a choice, so the third-person form is a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Grace might also supply inspiration for comedy

definitions.text: might also supply inspiration for comedy

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the three Graces of Greek myth

blocks.clueFragment: might also supply inspiration for comedy
blocks.note: second meaning: the Muse of comedy shares this name

explanation.surface: A woman named Grace could also provide comic inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace' looks like a woman's name; it is a Charite, and her namesake is a Muse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the name belongs both to one of the three Charites and to the Muse presiding over comedy.

clue.text: Not on coast but near it

definitions.text: Not on coast but near it

blocks.note: surface reading: somewhere inland, away from the beach
setter's reading: out at sea a short distance from land

explanation.surface: A paradoxical location that is close to the seaside without being on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on coast' first suggests inland, but the place is out in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Offshore means situated at sea some distance from the shore, like oil rigs and wind farms.

clue.text: The truth must be spoken on this

definitions.text: The truth must be spoken on this

blocks.clueFragment: The truth must be spoken on this
blocks.note: surface reading: a topic on which honesty is required
setter's reading: a witness swears a solemn promise in court, then must tell the truth

explanation.surface: A demand for honesty about some subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On this' sounds like 'about this subject' but means under this solemn promise, as in 'on my honour'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn sworn promise, such as a witness swearing to tell the truth in court.

clue.text: Waterways provide proper means of communication

blocks.note: first meaning: navigable stretches of water such as straits or canals
second meaning: official routes for messages, as in 'go through the proper ...'

explanation.surface: Rivers and canals are described as the right way to send messages.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers sea straits and canals as well as the official routes through which information is passed.

clue.text: His name was of importance on certain boards

definitions.text: His name was of importance on certain boards

blocks.clueFragment: His name was of importance on certain boards
blocks.note: surface reading: a man whose name mattered on company boards
setter's reading: the boards are the stage, and Wilde's comedy is about the importance of having this name

explanation.surface: A businessman's name carried weight on certain boards of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boards' means the stage; Oscar Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest turns on a man's need to be called this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Worthing in Wilde's comedy pretends to be named this, a pun on being earnest or serious.

clue.text: Abnormally excited by relic and hasty concealment

indicators.note: concealment disguises something, so the letters are put into a disguised arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets worked up over an ancient relic and a rushed attempt to hide it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterical describes a state of uncontrolled, extreme emotion or wild agitation.
